topic: The Impregnable Fortress: Understanding 256-bit Hash Security

sections.title: The Digital Fingerprint: What is a Hash?
lecture_lines: A hash function is like a digital blender.
It transforms any input into a unique string.
One small change creates a completely different hash.
animations: A white blender icon (#FFFFFF) labeled 'Hash Function' appears.
A blue cat image (#ADD8E6) enters the blender.
A light yellow hex string 'a591...' (#FFFFE0) appears on the right.
The cat image reappears with a red whisker (#FF0000) and enters the blender.
The hex string changes completely to a golden '3b2e...' (#FFD700).

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Binary Exponents
lecture_lines: Adding one bit doubles the total possible combinations.
Binary exponents grow at a staggering exponential rate.
256 bits provide a massive pool of unique values.
animations: A white '0' and '1' (#FFFFFF) appear for a 1-bit system.
A blue branching tree (#ADD8E6) quickly expands to represent exponential growth.
A long row of 256 gold light switches [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/switch.svg] (#FFD700) fades into the number '$2^{256}$'.

sections.title: Visualizing the Magnitude of $2^{256}$
lecture_lines: $2^{256}$ is roughly $1.15$ times $10^{77}$ combinations.
That is close to the atoms in the universe.
Imagine searching for one specific atom in space.
The scale spans from sand grains to entire galaxies.
Finding one specific hash is practically impossible.
animations: The number '$2^{256} \approx 1.15 \times 10^{77}$' (#FFFFFF) appears.
A light yellow dot 'Grain of Sand' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sand.svg] (#FFFFE0) zooms out to a beach.
Zoom out further to show a blue Earth [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/earth.svg] (#ADD8E6) in space.
Zoom out to show the golden Milky Way Galaxy (#FFD700).
A red dot (#FF0000) flashes in the galaxy, representing a single atom (hash).

sections.title: The Brute Force Challenge
lecture_lines: Brute force attempts every possible combination to crack.
Even billion-speed supercomputers cannot break it quickly.
It would take trillions of years to finish.
animations: A robot icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] (#FFFFFF) with a fast '1 Quadrillion H/s' counter (#ADD8E6).
A golden timer (#FFD700) counts up to trillions of years.
A red '0% complete' progress bar (#FF0000) appears for cracking the hash.

sections.title: Thermodynamic Limits: Why Math Defies Physics
lecture_lines: Flipping bits requires a specific amount of energy.
Computing every hash would consume the Sun's energy.
The oceans would boil before we reach 1 percent.
Security is guarded by the laws of thermodynamics.
This makes 256-bit hashes physically impossible to crack.
animations: A golden 'Energy Meter' (#FFD700) for the Sun [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sun.svg] appears at the top.
A white computer icon (#FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/computer.svg] starts processing combinations.
The meter drops to zero and the yellow Sun (#FFFF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sun.svg] fades to black.
Light blue 'Oceans Boil' text (#ADD8E6) appears with a steam effect.
A red '0.0001% complete' (#FF0000) flashes as the task fails.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Gold Standard of Security
lecture_lines: SHA-256 is the foundation of modern digital security.
Security depends on the vastness of the math space.
This mathematical fortress remains uncrackable by any means.
animations: White icons for Bitcoin [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bitcoin.svg] and a padlock [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/padlock.svg] (#FFFFFF) appear.
The blue detective (#ADD8E6) locks a digital chest.
A massive golden 'Mathematical Wall' (#FFD700) rises around the chest.
